groups.title: Explicit types
groups.check: Explicit types on the public API; no def combined with a type

groups.title: Numbers and money
groups.check: intdiv for integer division; money as BigDecimal with explicit scale and rounding

groups.title: Groovy truth, Elvis, safe navigation
groups.check: No Elvis where 0 or empty is valid; no safe navigation result assigned to a primitive; no File/Path truthiness meaning not-null

groups.title: Strings and GStrings
groups.check: No GString map keys and no GStrings without interpolation

groups.title: Null safety and boundaries
groups.check: Guard clauses at boundaries; empty collections instead of null

groups.title: Exceptions and logging
groups.check: Narrow catches, causes preserved, parameterised logging

groups.title: Security
groups.check: No Eval on input, no @Grab, parameterised SQL, list form process execution, default XML settings, bounded regexes

groups.title: Concurrency
groups.check: Shared state guarded; virtual threads for I/O

groups.title: Testing
groups.check: Spock specs use behaviour names, where: tables and with(obj)

groups.title: Style and CodeNarc
groups.check: CodeNarc clean; on Groovy 6, NullChecker strict and SqlInjectionChecker clean

groups.title: Groovy 5 and 6 compatibility
groups.check: Groovy 6-only constructs marked and kept out of code that must run on 5.x

groups.title: Runtime profile
groups.check: Constructs, parameter contracts, secrets and network calls as the runtime profile requires

groups.title: Naming
groups.check: Names say what things are and do: booleans as questions, verbs on methods, nouns on classes, no generic words, abbreviations or type prefixes, one verb per idea

groups.title: Gradle build scripts
groups.check: Tasks registered lazily, versions pinned, repositories over https only

entries.title: Integer division with /
entries.why: In Groovy `1 / 2` is 0.5 (a BigDecimal), unlike Java. Where the result is not narrowed to an integral type, code ported from Java that expects truncation silently gets a fraction; where it is narrowed (an int target, a cast, an int return), Groovy truncates anyway and nothing is reported.
entries.bad: def ratio = hits / total   // 0.25, a BigDecimal: fine; intdiv would make it 0
entries.good: int pages = total.intdiv(size)   // when truncation is meant; an int target truncates too
entries.fix: Use `a.intdiv(b)` when truncation is meant; this changes the value, so the bulk fix asks first.

entries.title: Elvis on a value where 0 or empty is valid
entries.why: Elvis uses Groovy truth, so `count ?: 10` replaces a legitimate 0 with the default. For a string or a collection the empty value is often absent in all but name, so there it is reported as information.
entries.good: int pageSize(Integer requested) { requested != null ? requested : 50 }
entries.fix: Compare with null explicitly: `x != null ? x : default`.

entries.title: Safe navigation into a primitive
entries.why: `a?.size()` is null when `a` is null; storing or returning that as a numeric primitive throws at run time. A `boolean` is left out: Groovy turns null into false there.
entries.fix: Supply a default with Elvis, or check for null first.

entries.title: File or Path used as a boolean
entries.why: Since Groovy 5 a File or Path is truthy only if it exists on disk (GROOVY-10949); code that meant 'is set' changes meaning.
entries.fix: Say which you mean: `file != null` (present) or `file.exists()` (`Files.exists(path)`) (exists on disk).

entries.title: GString in a log call
entries.why: A GString is built even when the level is disabled and may leak secrets into logs; parameterised messages are cheaper and safer.
entries.fix: Use '{}' placeholders and pass the values as arguments.

entries.title: Code evaluated from non-constant input
entries.why: Eval, GroovyShell and GroovyClassLoader compile and run their argument; on external input that is remote code execution. Groovy is not a sandbox.
entries.good: Use a data format (JSON, YAML) or a closed set of commands instead of evaluating code.
entries.fix: Do not evaluate input; parse data instead.

entries.title: @Grab in production code
entries.why: @Grab resolves and downloads dependencies at compile time; compilation is execution. Dependencies belong in Gradle with verification metadata.
entries.fix: Declare the dependency in the build (Gradle `implementation 'group:module:version'`) and remove the annotation.

entries.title: Command built as a string
entries.why: `"cmd $arg".execute()` splits on whitespace, so arguments with spaces or shell characters change the command.
entries.fix: Use the list form with validated arguments; never `sh -c` with input.

entries.title: XML DOCTYPE re-enabled
entries.why: Groovy's XML parsers reject DOCTYPE by default; enabling it on untrusted input exposes XXE.
entries.fix: Keep `allowDocTypeDeclaration` false and leave `disallow-doctype-decl` on.

entries.title: Groovy 6-only construct under a 5.x target
entries.why: `groovy.compat` lists a 5.x version, but this construct (val, @SafeRegex, groovy.typecheckers, dotted copyWith) does not compile on Groovy 5.
entries.good: final BigDecimal total = price * qty  // Groovy 6: val
entries.fix: Use the Groovy 5 form, or drop 5.x from `groovy.compat`.

entries.title: Spock .with {} in a condition block
entries.why: Groovy's `.with {}` is a plain method call, not a Spock condition block: the comparisons inside it are evaluated but never asserted, so a wrong value passes. Spock asserts each one only inside its own `with(obj) {}`.
entries.fix: Use Spock's `with(obj) { ... }`.

entries.title: Quoted interpolation in SQL
entries.why: Inside a GString passed to groovy.sql.Sql, `'$x'` is concatenated into the query text instead of bound as a parameter: SQL injection. Groovy 6 rejects it at run time; Groovy 5 only warns.
entries.fix: Remove the quotes around the interpolation so it is bound as a parameter.

entries.title: Stub on a private method
entries.why: Mockito and Spock doubles are generated subclasses: they cannot intercept a private method, so the real method runs. With Mockito the stubbing's matchers are left behind and fail an unrelated later stubbing.
entries.fix: Stub a package-private or public collaborator instead, or let the private method run with inputs that drive it.

entries.title: metaClass override that @CompileStatic code bypasses
entries.why: Calls inside @CompileStatic code are bound at compile time and never go through the metaClass, so the override does not apply to them and the test can pass without testing what it claims.
entries.fix: Stub a package-private or public seam with Mockito or Spock, or pass the collaborator in.

entries.title: metaClass on a test double
entries.why: A Mockito or Spock double intercepts calls through its generated class; a metaClass change on it applies only to dynamic Groovy calls through that reference. Two stubbing mechanisms on one object make the test depend on how each call is dispatched.
entries.fix: Stub the method through the double (doReturn/when, or Spock >>).

entries.title: Test without an assertion
entries.why: A JUnit test that neither asserts, verifies an interaction nor expects an exception passes whatever the code does; it adds coverage without checking behaviour.
entries.fix: Assert the result, verify the interaction that matters, or expect the exception (assertThrows).

entries.title: Missing dependencies (no classpath configured)
entries.why: Without a classpath, imports of library classes cannot resolve, so the compiler reports every import and every use of those classes as an error, and navigation, types and impact analysis stop at the unknown classes. The real cause is one missing setting, not many broken lines.
entries.good: groovyscope classpath   // writes the project's resolved classpath for the engine
entries.fix: Run `groovyscope classpath` (or set `workspace.classpath` in .groovyscope.yaml) so the engine sees the project's dependencies.

entries.title: Boolean without a question word
entries.why: A boolean named like a thing (`valid`, `flag`, `active`) reads as data; `isValid`, `hasChildren`, `canRetry` reads as the yes/no it is, at every call site. A Groovy property is left out: `boolean active` is already read as `isActive()`, and naming it `isActive` would give `isIsActive()`.
entries.fix: Start the name with is, has, can, should or another question word.

entries.title: Getter that changes state
entries.why: A caller of `getX()` expects a read. When it assigns a field, every reader of the call site is misled, and caches and tests built on the assumption break.
entries.fix: Name the method for the change it makes, or move the assignment out so the getter is side-effect free.

entries.title: Verb and noun swapped
entries.why: A class named with a verb (`ProcessOrder`) is a method in disguise; a public method named with a noun (`orderTotal()`) hides whether calling it computes, fetches or changes something.
entries.fix: Name classes for what they are and methods for what they do, starting with a verb.

entries.title: Name says nothing
entries.why: `data`, `info`, `tmp`, `obj`, `Manager`, `Helper`, `Util` describe every value or class equally well, so they describe none; the reader has to open the body to learn what it holds.
entries.fix: Name the thing for its content or role in this code.

entries.title: Abbreviation or single letter
entries.why: `cfg`, `mgr`, `svc`, `ctx` and a lone `x` outside a loop save keystrokes once and cost a lookup on every read, and spell checkers, search and agents miss them.
entries.fix: Spell the word out; loop indexes, lambda parameters and the abbreviations the team lists under naming.allowedAbbreviations are fine.

entries.title: Type encoded in the name
entries.why: `strName`, `intCount`, `m_field`, `arrItems` repeat the declared type and go stale when the type changes; Groovy's static types already say it.
entries.fix: Drop the prefix and let the declaration carry the type.

entries.title: Name contradicts the type
entries.why: A `Map` called `userList`, a `String` called `retryCount`, a `String` called `expiryDate`, a plural name on a single value: the name promises one shape and the type delivers another, so callers write the wrong code.
entries.fix: Rename to match the type, or change the type to match the promise.

entries.title: Mixed vocabulary for one idea
entries.why: `getUser`, `fetchAccount`, `loadProfile` and `retrieveOrder` in one class make callers guess which verb this code uses; one verb per idea makes names predictable.
entries.bad: User getUser(); Account fetchAccount(); Profile loadProfile()
entries.good: User getUser(); Account getAccount(); Profile getProfile()
entries.fix: Pick one verb per idea (naming.vocabulary records the choice) and rename the others through rename.

entries.title: Interaction in then: without a cardinality, or a double created there
entries.why: In a then: block Spock treats `mock.call() >> value` as a stub, not a check, so the feature passes whether or not the call happens; a Mock() created in then: exists only after when: has run, so no interaction can reach it.
entries.fix: Give the interaction a cardinality (`1 * mock.call()`), or move stubs and doubles to given:.

entries.title: Data table column unused or declared twice
entries.why: A where: column that the feature never reads (and its name never shows as `#column`) feeds values that test nothing; a column declared twice makes Spock reject the specification, which the analysis compile does not report.
entries.bad:
expect:
a + b == c

where:
a | b | c | d
1 | 2 | 3 | 9
entries.good:
expect:
a + b == c

where:
a | b || c
1 | 2 || 3
entries.fix: Use the column in the feature or its name, or remove it; rename a duplicated column.

entries.title: @Unroll without a name pattern
entries.why: Spock 2 unrolls every data driven feature by default, so `@Unroll` with no pattern does nothing and only suggests otherwise to the reader.
entries.fix: Remove it, or keep it only with a name pattern.

entries.title: Exception condition outside then:, or two in one then: block
entries.why: Spock accepts `thrown()`, `notThrown()` and `noExceptionThrown()` only in a then: block, and only one per block; anything else makes Spock reject the specification at compile time, which the analysis compile (without Spock's transformation) does not report.
entries.good:
when:
store.save('')

then:
def e = thrown(IllegalArgumentException)
e.message == 'key'
entries.fix: Put the call that throws in when: and the exception condition in the then: after it; keep one per then: block.

entries.title: Eager task API
entries.why: `task x { }` and `tasks.create` create and configure the task in every build, even when it never runs, which slows configuration and defeats Gradle's lazy task configuration.
entries.fix: Declare tasks with `tasks.register`, and look them up with `tasks.named`.

entries.title: Dynamic dependency version
entries.why: A version such as `1.+`, `latest.release` or a range `[1.0,2.0)` resolves to whatever is newest on the day of the build, so two builds of one commit can differ and a release can pull in a breaking or compromised artefact.
entries.fix: Pin the version; a platform (BOM) or a version catalogue keeps the pins in one place, and dependency locking records them.

entries.title: Insecure or machine local repository
entries.why: A repository over plain `http://` lets anyone on the network path replace artefacts; `mavenLocal()` lets whatever was last installed on this machine shadow the published artefacts, so builds differ between machines. The http case is an error, mavenLocal() a warning.
entries.fix: Use https:// repositories; publish to a real repository instead of relying on mavenLocal(), or limit it with a content filter.

entries.title: Possible null dereference (Groovy 6 NullChecker)
entries.why: The checker proves at compile time that a value may be null where it is dereferenced. In strict mode it needs no annotations.
entries.good:
String s = map.get(key)
if (s != null) { s.length() }
entries.fix: Guard with a null check, Elvis, requireNonNull, or annotate the contract.

entries.title: SQL built from untrusted text (Groovy 6 SqlInjectionChecker)
entries.why: The checker flags queries assembled from strings that are not bound parameters.
entries.bad: sql.rows('SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = ' + id)
entries.fix: Bind values as parameters.

entries.title: Side effect in a @Pure method (Groovy 6 PurityChecker)
entries.why: @Pure methods must not modify state; the checker verifies it so the method is a self-contained specification for humans and agents.
entries.fix: Remove the side effect or drop @Pure.

entries.title: Modification outside @Modifies (Groovy 6 ModifiesChecker)
entries.why: The method changes state it does not declare in @Modifies.
entries.bad: @Modifies({ this.items }) void add(String s) { items << s; size++ }
entries.good: @Modifies({ [this.items, this.size] }) void add(String s) { items << s; size++ }
entries.fix: Declare every modified field in @Modifies.

entries.title: Invalid or risky regex (Groovy 6 RegexChecker)
entries.why: The checker validates regex literals at compile time.
entries.fix: Fix the pattern; bound regexes on input with @SafeRegex.

entries.title: Format string does not match its arguments
entries.why: The checker verifies String.format-style calls at compile time.
entries.fix: Match the format specifiers to the argument types.

entries.title: Non-associative combiner in injectParallel
entries.why: A parallel reduction needs an associative combiner or results differ run to run.
entries.fix: Use an associative combiner.

entries.title: Class without a static compilation choice
entries.why: Most Groovy defects come from dynamic dispatch; @CompileStatic removes them and is the main performance lever.
entries.fix: Add @CompileStatic; where dynamic dispatch is needed (builders, DSLs), add @CompileDynamic on the smallest method and say why.

entries.title: def instead of a type
entries.why: `def` is Object; on public API it hides the contract and defeats static checking.
entries.bad: def compute(def a, def b) { a + b }
entries.good: BigDecimal compute(BigDecimal a, BigDecimal b) { a + b }
entries.fix: Replace def with the concrete type; locals may use var when the type is obvious.

entries.title: Method without a return type
entries.why: Public methods carry explicit types so callers and the type checker know the contract.
entries.fix: Declare the return type.

entries.title: Parameter without a type
entries.why: Untyped parameters accept anything and defeat static checking.
entries.fix: Declare the parameter type.

entries.title: def combined with a type
entries.why: `def String x` is redundant: def is Object, and the type already declares the variable.
entries.fix: Remove def.

entries.title: Double quotes without interpolation
entries.why: Single quotes give a String; double quotes are for interpolation.
entries.fix: Use single quotes.

entries.title: GString used as a map key
entries.why: A GString key is not equal to the String with the same content and its hash code is unstable.
entries.fix: Call .toString() on interpolated keys.

entries.title: ${} inside single quotes
entries.why: '${x}' is a literal string; the interpolation was almost certainly meant.
entries.fix: Use double quotes.

entries.title: Null returned instead of an empty collection
entries.why: Callers then need null checks; an empty collection is safe to iterate.
entries.fix: Return an empty collection.

entries.title: Catching Exception
entries.why: A broad catch hides unrelated failures; catch Exception only in a top-level handler.
entries.good: catch (NoSuchFileException e) { throw new IllegalStateException('config not found', e) }
entries.fix: Catch the narrowest type and rethrow with the cause.

entries.title: Empty catch block
entries.why: A swallowed exception hides the failure.
entries.fix: Handle, log with the exception, or rethrow with the cause.

entries.title: println in production code
entries.why: Use a logger with levels and parameterised messages.
entries.fix: Use @Slf4j and parameterised logging.

entries.title: new BigDecimal(double)
entries.why: The double is already imprecise; the BigDecimal keeps the error.
entries.fix: Use a literal, the G suffix or BigDecimal.valueOf.

entries.title: java.util.Random for security
entries.why: Random is predictable; tokens and keys need SecureRandom.
entries.fix: Use SecureRandom.

entries.title: Private field could be final
entries.why: Fields assigned once should say so; final documents and enforces it.
entries.fix: Make the field final.

entries.title: Construct the runtime has not accepted
entries.why: The runtime profile lists this construct as blocked, unproven, discouraged or proven only in another service; a local green build does not show what the runtime will do.
entries.fix: Use the replacement the profile names, or prove the construct on the runtime first.

entries.title: Newer Groovy than the runtime runs
entries.why: The governed file compiles on the runtime's older Groovy; this construct needs a newer one.
entries.fix: Use the older form, or raise the runtime's Groovy version first.

entries.title: Descriptor value the runtime rejects
entries.why: The runtime does not accept this descriptor value.
entries.fix: Use one of the values the profile allows.

entries.title: Parameter read that the descriptor does not declare
entries.why: The accessor names a parameter the descriptor does not declare, so the runtime never supplies it.
entries.fix: Declare the parameter in the descriptor or fix the name.

entries.title: Accessor type differs from the descriptor
entries.why: The parameter is declared with one type and read as another.
entries.fix: Read it with the type the descriptor declares.

entries.title: Fallback on a declared parameter
entries.why: The descriptor supplies every declared parameter before the code runs, so a ?: fallback is dead code and a second, drifting default.
entries.fix: Remove the fallback; keep the default in the descriptor.

entries.title: Raw map read of a declared parameter
entries.why: The raw parameter map is untyped; the typed accessor checks the declaration.
entries.fix: Use the typed accessor.

entries.title: Second validation of a descriptor parameter
entries.why: Validation belongs with the descriptor parameter; an infrastructure validation block duplicates and drifts.
entries.fix: Remove the validation block from the infrastructure variable.

entries.title: Default on a descriptor-supplied infrastructure variable
entries.why: The descriptor supplies the value, so an infrastructure default is never used and misleads readers.
entries.fix: Keep type and description only.

entries.title: Frozen contract changed
entries.why: Parameter names, output keys, exception texts and method signatures are relied on outside this code; the baseline recorded them.
entries.fix: Restore the recorded item, or update the baseline deliberately (groovyscope baseline save) once the change is agreed.

entries.title: Test seam made unreachable
entries.why: Tests stub this method through instance dispatch; making it private or static silently disables the stub.
entries.fix: Keep the method non-private and non-static.

entries.title: Secret flows into a log, exception, map or output
entries.why: Secrets must not reach logs, exception text, parameter maps or outputs.
entries.fix: Keep secrets in the secret store and pass references, not values.

entries.title: Library capability rewritten by hand
entries.why: The runtime's library already provides this; hand-written versions drift from it.
entries.fix: Use the library capability the hint names.

entries.title: Network call outside the designated methods
entries.why: Retries, timeouts and logging live in a few designated methods; calls elsewhere bypass them.
entries.fix: Route the call through one of the designated methods.

entries.title: Does not compile on the runtime's Groovy
entries.why: The emulation compile with the runtime's Groovy version and classpath failed.
entries.fix: Fix the reported error before publishing.
